The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

In the provided text, the central conflict arises from the clash between economic greed and cultural preservation. Jacob, a prospector, discovers a vast gold deposit on land that is sacred to the local indigenous tribe. This discovery creates a direct opposition between Jacob’s potential financial gain and the tribe chief’s determination to protect his people's heritage. The conflict escalates when outsiders become aware of the gold, forcing Jacob to face a moral dilemma regarding where his loyalties truly lie—between his own interests and the rights and traditions of the indigenous community.
